records.sourceAnchor: Guideline pages 3-15 (PDF pages 3-15): PC/APC routes, grant ceilings, eligibility, exclusions, funding-use restrictions, project duration and monitoring; official programme page key features
observations: The March 2026 guideline positions NIDHI PRAYAS 2.0 as a pre-incubation prototype programme implemented through selected PRAYAS Centres (PCs) and Advance PRAYAS Centres (APCs), with SINE, IIT Bombay as the national PMU. This is a centre-mediated route, not a direct universal grant portal.

The guideline sets a maximum of ₹20 lakh per innovator/startup at a PC and ₹40 lakh at an APC, with the final amount decided through the applicable local monitoring process. The project term is 15 months, with a possible six-month extension subject to approval; the programme page independently describes the PC/APC support model.

An applicant may be an individual without a registered startup or an early-stage startup, must show ownership or licensed rights to the relevant IP, be at least 18 and an Indian citizen, and may use the programme only once. A startup must be incorporated in India for no more than five years, have at least 51% Indian-citizen ownership and turnover not exceeding ₹1 crore in any financial year since incorporation.

The fine print excludes pure software, e-commerce, service and app-based solutions, and excludes parallel NIDHI-EIR support for the same or similar idea. The guideline also imposes prior-funding disclosure, cumulative government-support limits, prototype-stage restrictions, milestone/full-time commitments, possible recovery of unused funds, and restrictions on use of funds.

The official page and March 2026 guideline do not establish a currently open applicant deadline for every innovator. The public record must therefore distinguish programme existence from a currently open PC/APC call and must route users to a verified designated centre or current call before presenting an actionable application.

The record must not combine PC/APC centre-level allocations with the individual innovator ceiling, and must not advertise the ₹20 lakh/₹40 lakh ceilings as guaranteed awards. It must also distinguish the beneficiary route from the separate DST call for incubators seeking to establish or operate a PC/APC.

publicationGuard.reason: The March 2026 guideline is current first-party evidence, but the user-facing route depends on designated PC/APC availability and a verified live call; the current programme-versus-window distinction and supersession review must be completed before publication.
